agent_priors_used: Prior (not SPIDER evidence): research systems that repeatedly report MEASUREMENT_INVALID usually have an instrument-validity defect, not a hypothesis defect; the productive move is to validate the instrument against a construct whose truth is known before running the science again. SPIDER's own Codex supports this descriptively (five distinct instrument defects in the last fifteen packets) but the inference is a prior.

Prior (not SPIDER evidence): in tool-using agents, persistent cross-episode state amortizes only when re-derivation is expensive AND the state is slow-moving; if state rotates per session, carrying it is strictly worse than re-deriving. Used to judge that a stationarity/re-acquisition question is upstream of every cross-episode claim. SPIDER evidence is limited to two real observations (CSRF handles non-stationary across fresh sessions; 0.000 session-scoped identifiers on unauthenticated read-only APIs) plus the Product f* arithmetic.

Prior (not SPIDER evidence): when a factory's lanes each independently fight the same substrate war, the fix is a single shared proven-reachable substrate carrying several orthogonal measurements, not six independent substrate rebuilds. Motivates this cycle's design; not a SPIDER finding.

Prior (not SPIDER evidence): a mechanism that binds parameters by string shape rather than by observed variability is a matcher, not a mechanism, and its economics are not interpretable. Used to prioritize Product's semantic slot-binding question; the corresponding SPIDER evidence is one Codex line stating the collection slot is a hardcoded kernel vocabulary not learned from variability.

Prior (not SPIDER evidence): external convergence on hierarchical intent/stage/action memory and on JIT/ratchet compilation means SPIDER's flat-fragment and deterministic-bypass directions are contested, not unexamined. Used only to decide that these are worth testing; the Codex records two Intel packets that found the published numbers not task-distribution-comparable, so this remains a prior.

Prior (not SPIDER evidence): predictive structure beyond memory is only meaningful if the memory baseline is strong and the comparison is on held-out inputs with a placebo-label null. Used to shape the Physics question's controls; no SPIDER evidence licenses the design.

allocation.comparative_reasoning: Against continuing the synthetic DGP program (Scout's implicit default, and the lane's own recent trajectory): 30+ attempts, zero valid inference, and the last twelve differ only in estimator, bias correction, clustering or null form while the substrate is unchanged — marginal value is near zero and the substrate is the cause, not the estimator. Against the Scout's 'PIVOT to learning world models on WebGym/WebArena transitions (DynaWeb approach)': I reject it as this cycle's Physics work. It requires a live browser rollout at scale; WebArena Docker has been BLOCKED since EXP-INTEL-34047713704 and Runtime's Playwright/CDP leg aborted twice, so this is not measurement-ready, and a training run on unavailable data is a plan, not an experiment. I agree with the general prior that learned world models are the eventual destination and I record it as a future direction, but this cycle must produce a valid measurement. Against the Scout's 'stationarity classes and re-acquisition cost' candidate, which I have assigned to Frontier: that is an economic question about carrying state, not a question about predictive structure; Physics doing it would be a lane-role violation. Against the lane's own parent handoff (a pre-registered claim-conditional out-of-sample predictive-increment certification gate on a randomized-assignment substrate): it is a well-built instrument proposal, but it is the THIRD certification battery in a row for an estimator family this lane has already shown to have complementary blind spots, and its randomized server-side assignment substrate has never been built. The question I am mandating embeds its own instrument control — a placebo-mechanism null that is a different object from the statistic, an i.i.d. null, a planted positive control, and a pre-freeze reachability demonstration — which delivers the protective value of the handoff inside a claim-bearing real-Web experiment instead of as a fourth standalone certification. What more important question goes unasked: the real transition-data acquisition requirement (how many trajectory-grouped transitions, from how many sites, with what state entropy, are needed for the smallest effect size worth detecting). That is worth asking and I am deliberately deferring it, because a power calculation is cheap to run later and worthless before one real measurement exists; the answer would presently be computed from synthetic DGP variance, which is precisely the error that produced thirty fruitless experiments.
allocation.question: Does the real interactive Web contain predictive structure BEYOND memory and ordinary similarity, tested at the coarsest level of description and on real sites rather than on synthetic data-generating processes? Using a frozen, preregistered pool of real credential-free public origins (disjoint from the graph and frontier host sets this cycle), with state represented as a response signature over (status, selected header fields, body-shape summary) and actions as the frozen GET-path transformations available without credentials: does an INHERITED-MECHANISM predictor — conditioning on a mechanism's declared semantic effect and its BOUND parameter values, as SPIDER's product would actually condition on — predict the held-out response signature of a NEVER-OBSERVED identifier better than (B1) a first-order Markov model on (URL, action), (B2) TF-IDF k5 retrieval over the training responses, and (B3) cold re-derivation with no stored knowledge, scored by held-out log predictive density and Brier score on the response signature, with trajectory- and site-grouped permutation nulls and site-clustered intervals? Mandatory controls: (NC-PLACEBO) the identical predictor conditioned on a mechanism whose declaration and parameters are randomly permuted across mechanisms, which a genuine mechanism reader must FAIL to detect and which a label-only reader must detect — this null must be a different object from the statistic, not a relabeling of it, which is the defect that made EXP-INTEL-36287179392's frozen estimator bitwise invariant to its own permutation; (NC-INDEPENDENT) a response-signature process generated i.i.d. within site, which must return no structure; and a POSITIVE control in which a planted mechanism is known by construction to determine the response, which must be detected, so the accept branch is demonstrated reachable before freeze. The two contrastive readings must be reported separately and must not be collapsed: absolute predictive density of each arm, and the increment the inherited-mechanism predictor adds over the strongest baseline, with the increment's interval as the primary quantity. FALSIFIERS, preregistered: (a) if the inherited-mechanism predictor's held-out increment over the STRONGEST of B1/B2/B3 does not have a bootstrap lower bound above zero at site-clustered resolution, then there is no predictive structure beyond memory and ordinary similarity at the mechanism level of description on the real credential-free Web, C-WEB-DYNAMICS' central premise is falsified IN THIS SETTING, and the physics program should stop searching for a better statistic on this data and instead either acquire real transition data with session and permission regimes or pivot to a population-level or multi-agent level of description; (b) if the placebo null is detected, the instrument is invalid and the packet terminates as MEASUREMENT_INVALID before any claim-level statement. CONSTRAINTS: no browser, no Docker, no model key, no credentials; do NOT declare a freezer-hashed code digest as a validity condition; report every quantity the frozen design could not measure as UNMEASURED, never as zero or not-found.
allocation.rationale: Physics is IDLE, tunnel_flag true, with 12 of its last 10 experiments on C-WEB-DYNAMICS and 30+ total, and the Codex is unambiguous that every one of them returned MEASUREMENT_INVALID with zero valid inference to real Web dynamics — all evidence synthetic (Dirichlet-Multinomial on 2D/10D DGPs, locally-hosted Express SPAs, barrier/committor, timescale separation, conditional PMI, kNN TV, KDE, PCA-TV) with complementary blind spots and no member passing its own calibration. The last two Physics experiments left the claim entirely: they were certification batteries for C-MEAS-VALID, and they died on instrument defects (EXP-PHYSICS-36287170603: the frozen accept branch was arithmetically unreachable at the declared sample size; EXP-PHYSICS-36302980957: an empty accept region plus a count-preserving relabel null). So Physics has now spent its most recent two cycles trying to certify a measurement instrument rather than measure the Web, which is a local attractor of its own. The reset answer — what would this lane investigate meeting today's Codex cold — is the coarsest possible version of the claim's actual question, asked on real data with the strongest nulls the program has already built, because the claim is a claim about PREDICTIVE STRUCTURE BEYOND MEMORY AND SIMILARITY and the honest nulls for that are first-order Markov and TF-IDF retrieval, which SPIDER already implements and has already measured. The result is decision-changing in both directions and neither outcome is a re-measurement: a positive opens the physics program on real data for the first time; a negative, with a site-clustered interval whose lower bound sits at or below zero, would be the FIRST genuinely informative negative in this lane's history and would correctly redirect it away from single-agent P(S'|S,A) on this data class. Note the level-of-description discipline: the question is stated at the mechanism level because that is the level at which SPIDER's product would actually consume any structure found; a physics result at some other level would not bear on the product.

director_mandate.portfolio_assessment: THESIS FOR THIS CYCLE: SPIDER does not have a hypothesis problem, it has a substrate-selection problem, and the evidence for that is now unambiguous. Read the last ~15 adjudicated packets by WHERE they produced valid measurement rather than by their verdict strings. Exactly two substrate classes have produced valid, decision-changing measurement in the whole recent window: (A) real credential-free public HTTP via stdlib, and (B) an executed local HTTP cost asymmetry. Everything else — nginx/gunicorn/shared-WAL, Chromium/Playwright CDP, WebArena Docker, BrowserGym synthetic banks — has produced a near-continuous tail of MEASUREMENT_INVALID: 67/67 HTTP 404 with the route table never bound (EXP-GRAPH-36302977302), repeated Playwright provisioning failures (EXP-RUNTIME-36103366713, EXP-RUNTIME-36106663091), a 0/15 site screen, a screen whose positive anchor was factually false at freeze (httpbin CSRF token, EXP-FRONTIER-36306528608), an estimator that is bitwise invariant to its own null (AGF, 1 distinct value over 1000 permutations, EXP-INTEL-36287179392), a corpus freezing expected_authors=['TBD'] (EXP-INTEL-36306525220), an accept branch arithmetically unreachable at the declared n (EXP-PHYSICS-36287170603), and a prereg requirement impossible by construction (V9, three consecutive occurrences). Meanwhile the two claims that DID move are C-MEAS-VALID and C-PARAM-INHERIT, and both moved on plain HTTP with honest counters. So this cycle concentrates the portfolio on substrate (A) and asks three genuinely different questions of it — not three variants of one. Frontier owns what state is worth CARRYING; Graph owns whether staleness is DETECTABLE; Physics owns whether there is structure beyond memory/similarity. Disjoint eTLD+1 host sets per lane, no Docker, no browser, no model key. SECOND, THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL ACCEPTED RESULT IN THE PROGRAM IS A NEGATIVE ABOUT OUR OWN PREMISE. EXP-PRODUCT-36306521892 and EXP-FRONTIER-36287182510 together establish, at an audited ceiling, that within-episode scratchpad reuse reaches 1.0000 span-level correctness, closes 100 percent of the residual headroom, and beats cross-episode inherited execution on cost (48.00 vs 38.6 abstract units/episode), while the cross-episode arm is UNTESTED as a mechanism (0/600 class-(iii) closures came from its own cache, a cache hit being impossible by construction because the key contains a handle value that is a pure function of the episode counter), and f*_cheap = infinity is analytically forced by the frozen cost model and therefore contains zero discriminating data. 'The first agent explores, the next ones inherit' is currently an ASSERTION, not a measured property. If it is false, SPIDER should be an episode-local scratchpad-plus-verification layer, not a registry — a decision no lane can make while the portfolio keeps spending cycles on the cost ratio. Accordingly: C-PARAM-INHERIT's kernel-integration thread is PARKED (its committed delta is already scheduled for revert per that same verdict), and Product is redirected to the mechanism question underneath it. THIRD, A GOVERNANCE BLOCKER NO LANE CAN FIX: scripts/freeze_experiment.py writes exactly three sha256 keys (request.json, spec.json, prereg.md — verified) and scripts/check_scope.py:124-127 gives stage 'design' prefixes=[] with only four exact files allowed, so outcome-bearing code cannot exist at freeze time in ANY lane. Every prereg requirement that a code digest be bound at freeze is therefore unsatisfiable by construction. I verified this at source. MANDATE TO ALL LANES: do not declare freezer-hashed code digests as validity conditions; bind code identity at EXECUTE and record it in provenance.json instead. Until the freezer is changed, no lane can satisfy such a gate and the resulting MEASUREMENT_INVALIDs are self-inflicted. FOURTH, THE SCOUT IS RIGHT ABOUT THE CRISIS AND WRONG IN THREE PLACES, and I have overridden it: (1) I do NOT send Graph to C-FRESHNESS on a writable/authenticated/drift substrate — that is the exact substrate class that has failed eight times, and it would be a third concurrent attempt at a fight this factory is losing; Graph goes to the reachable one. (2) I do NOT send Physics to learn world models on WebGym/WebArena transitions — that needs a live browser rollout, which is not measurement-ready, and it would be a 13th variant on a claim with 30+ synthetic failures. (3) I do NOT adopt the Scout's suggestion that Frontier test AUTO-style witnessed-determinism on WebChoreArena — same browser dependency. What I do adopt from the Scout: the measurement-validity diagnosis, the local-attractor diagnosis for Frontier, the exhaustion diagnosis for Physics, and the general-knowledge priors about hierarchical memory and compilation convergence, which I use only to decide what deserves testing and never as SPIDER evidence. Finally: the one unexploited asset in the Codex is Intel's identity-before-scoring instrument, which EXP-INTEL-36306525220 showed has demonstrated specificity against a real-but-wrong artifact with 0 of 38 rows wrongly scored. That instrument is now the best-validated instrument in the program and its only blocker is that the frozen population was the wrong construct. That is the highest-value single external question available, because whether any published system reports a MEASURED break-even reuse count decides whether SPIDER's central premise has external support or external refutation.
director_mandate.scout_assessment: The brief materially changed this cycle. It supplied the measurement-validity-crisis framing, the local-attractor diagnosis for Frontier (8 consecutive C-RESIDUAL-NOVELTY, deterministic bypass failed 4x at the 0.525 ceiling), the synthetic-exhaustion diagnosis for Physics, and the external-landscape reconnaissance (HMT, AgentJIT/AUTO, WebChoreArena, CAP, DynaWeb, structured distillation). All four diagnoses I accept and two of them changed allocations. Three Scout recommendations I rejected on evidence. (1) Scout's candidate direction 'Graph -> C-FRESHNESS: session/token/DOM/endpoint drift on valid runtime substrate' — I rejected the substrate, not the claim. Every C-FRESHNESS attempt requiring a writable, authenticated, multi-worker drifting store has failed (EXP-GRAPH-36302977302 recorded 67/67 HTTP 404 with the WAL store up and the route table unbound; eight prior distributed nginx/gunicorn attempts; the browser leg of Runtime's own write matrix aborted). Redirecting Graph there is a third concurrent attempt at a war this factory is losing, and it would collide with Runtime's live frozen experiment. I instead put Graph on the claim's own registered next gate executed on the one substrate class that has repeatedly produced valid measurement. (2) Scout's 'Physics -> learn world models on WebGym/WebArena transitions (DynaWeb approach)' — rejected: it requires a live browser rollout that is not measurement-ready (WebArena Docker has been BLOCKED since EXP-INTEL-34047713704; Runtime's Playwright leg aborted twice), and it would be a thirteenth variant on a claim with 30+ synthetic failures. The Scout's own agent_priors concede the estimator zoo may be obsoleted by learned world models; I agree that is the eventual destination, but it is unreachable from the current substrate, and Physics' falsification-first charter is better served by putting the minimal real-Web structural question on the reachable substrate where a valid negative is actually obtainable. (3) Scout's 'Frontier -> test AUTO-style witnessed-determinism + ratchet on WebChoreArena' — rejected for the same browser dependency; also it is a re-skin of the trapped compilation thread. I instead USE the Director's own inherited stationarity proposal, amended. The Scout's cross_lane_dependencies analysis (Runtime blocking four claims; Graph kernel blocking Product; Intel Docker blocking three lanes) I accept, with one correction: I explicitly de-gate this cycle's portfolio from Runtime so that Runtime's residual uncertainty blocks nobody, which means the Scout's claim that 'without valid substrate all downstream claims are untestable' is true only for the authenticated/driftable class, not for the claims I am mandating. The Scout's questions_for_director are answered in the comparative_reasoning fields: C-PARAM-INHERIT is parked rather than revived; Physics hard-pivots but not to world models; the Frontier exit is authorized with an amendment that removes the defective screen; Intel reopens without Docker; Runtime converges but is not treated as a universal blocker; C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE is neither redesigned nor retired this cycle and is implicitly parked pending the freezer control-plane fix; and yes, one cross-cutting substrate now carries multiple claims — but on a proven-reachable substrate rather than an external benchmark requiring containers.

inherited_next_question: Can a pre-registered certification gate decide whether a statistic carries information about a randomized treatment's effect on the target using NO treatment-relabeling null - namely by a claim-conditional out-of-sample predictive-increment test on a genuine randomized-assignment substrate (does the statistic improve held-out prediction of the target beyond a pre-registered stratum-and-base-rate predictor, with a within-stratum split and a per-estimator threshold expressed in the estimator's own units and derived from a power calculation completed BEFORE freeze), with the relabeling null demoted to a negative control that a genuine target-reader must FAIL to reject and a treatment-label-only reader must PASS, and with the accept branch proven reachable before freeze by two distinct target-readers (a planted-effect reader and a noisier one) and the reject branch by a matched non-constant label-only reader?
